datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: CRISM Full Resolution Targeted (FRT) observation over Columbia Hills: FRT00003192_07
datasets.instrument_sensor: CRISM (Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars)
datasets.measurement_observable: Hyperspectral radiance modeled for atmospheric correction; retrieved surface Lambert albedo/reflectance spectra
datasets.wavelength_bandpass: 0.4–4.0 µm (545 bands); false-color composite uses 1098 nm (blue), 1518 nm (green), 2528 nm (red)
datasets.data_type_product_type: Hyperspectral image cube (FRT mode); retrieved surface spectra (Lambert albedos)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Acquired while Spirit was located at the Low Ridge winter campaign site
datasets.location_coverage: Columbia Hills and surrounding plains in Gusev Crater; ~10 km frame width; Mars equirectangular projection (as used in figures)
datasets.how_used: Primary orbital dataset analyzed; radiative transfer (DISORT) used to atmospherically correct CRISM radiances and retrieve surface spectra; searched for hydrated mineral bands and evaluated endmember mixing (Husband Hill/Tennessee Valley bright ripples vs El Dorado dark ripples).

datasets.how_used: Used as the intensity (pan-sharpening) layer to sharpen fine detail in a CRISM-based false-color infrared composite map of the Columbia Hills.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: HiRISE image base used for traverse/experiment mapping: PSP_001513_1655_red
datasets.target_name: Mars (Gusev Crater, Columbia Hills / Home Plate region)

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer (TES) data over Gusev plains
datasets.measurement_observable: Thermal emission spectra used for surface composition/thermophysical interpretation

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Spirit rover Mini-TES emission spectra used for rock/soil spectral classes and comparisons (Voltaire region, ripples, vesicular rocks)
datasets.measurement_observable: Thermal infrared emissivity spectra; atmospheric temperature profiles (for CRISM modeling context)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Includes Voltaire campaign (Mini-TES footprints shown for sol 551 scene) and later operations; also notes Mini-TES recalibration using Gertrude Weise disturbed soil during sols 1292–1304
datasets.location_coverage: Voltaire outcrops/float rocks; Cliffhanger and El Dorado ripple surfaces; Low Ridge vesicular rocks (Esperanza and others)
datasets.how_used: Used to (1) classify Voltaire-region rocks into spectral classes (e.g., Wishstone-like, Backstay-like, Adirondack-like, Descartes class, Assemblee class), (2) compare ripple surface spectra (dust-dominated vs olivine-dominated), and (3) compare vesicular rock spectra (Esperanza and others) to a pyroxene-rich spectral shape; also referenced as providing atmospheric temperature profiles to support CRISM radiative transfer modeling.

queries.query: Use Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CRISM full-resolution targeted hyperspectral cubes over the Columbia Hills in Gusev Crater (∼18 m/pixel; 0.4–4.0 µm) to retrieve surface Lambert albedo/reflectance after atmospheric correction and quantify spectral endmember mixing between bright dust-coated ripple surfaces on Husband Hill/Tennessee Valley and darker mafic ripple fields near El Dorado.

Start from the raw Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CRISM full-resolution targeted radiance measurements over the Columbia Hills acquired during the Spirit Low Ridge winter season to independently propagate aerosols and gas absorption through radiative-transfer atmospheric correction, then assess detectability limits for weak hydration-related absorptions in the 1.9–2.5 µm region.

queries.query: Assemble Mars Express OMEGA hyperspectral reflectance observations over the Gusev crater plains (regional scale) in the 0.4–5 µm range to quantify the spectral mixing between slightly oxidized basaltic sands and surface dust at ~350 m/pixel sampling.

Use Mars Express OMEGA derived global map products from 0.4–5 µm to place the Gusev crater plains spectral endmembers (mafic sands versus ferric-rich dust) into a planet-wide compositional context suitable for comparison with other low-albedo and dust-mantled regions.

output_parsed.paper_title: Spirit Mars Rover Mission to the Columbia Hills, Gusev Crater: Mission overview and selected results from the Cumberland Ridge to Home Plate

queries.query: Assemble a Spirit rover Microscopic Imager dataset suitable for quantifying clast morphology and matrix microtexture in Columbia Hills bedrock exposures at Gusev Crater (e.g., conglomeratic/impact-melt candidates on Husband Hill), emphasizing in-situ close-up frames that preserve mm-scale texture for grain-size and rounding statistics.

Compile Spirit rover Microscopic Imager products for quantitative grain-size and grain-shape analysis of platy, granular outcrops in the Columbia Hills (Low Ridge winter-campaign vicinity), prioritizing calibrated MI image products appropriate for measuring coarse sand-sized grains and resolving surface microrelief under variable illumination.

queries.query: Assemble Spirit rover Mini-TES thermal-IR emissivity spectra (5–29 µm) acquired within Gusev Crater’s Columbia Hills to discriminate dust-dominated versus mafic sand surfaces and to derive spectral endmembers for altered/glassy outcrops relative to basaltic rocks.

Use Spirit rover Mini-TES brightness-temperature products for Columbia Hills observations in Gusev Crater to quantify surface temperature variability needed to convert radiance to emissivity consistently and to support thermal/near-IR radiative-transfer comparisons with orbital spectroscopy.

queries.query: Assemble Opportunity rover Mini-TES averaged, mirror-dust–corrected thermal-IR emissivity spectra for Meridiani Planum rock targets (including Bounce Rock) to use as a pyroxene-dominated reference library for comparison against vesicular basalt spectra from other rover sites.

Extract Opportunity rover Mini-TES reduced-data (RDR) thermal emission spectra of Meridiani Planum rocks to independently verify the pyroxenite-like spectral shape of Bounce Rock and quantify pyroxene versus olivine contributions in the 5–29 µm region.

final_output.query: Use Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CRISM full-resolution targeted hyperspectral cubes over the Columbia Hills in Gusev Crater (∼18 m/pixel; 0.4–4.0 µm) to retrieve surface Lambert albedo/reflectance after atmospheric correction and quantify spectral endmember mixing between bright dust-coated ripple surfaces on Husband Hill/Tennessee Valley and darker mafic ripple fields near El Dorado.

Start from the raw Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CRISM full-resolution targeted radiance measurements over the Columbia Hills acquired during the Spirit Low Ridge winter season to independently propagate aerosols and gas absorption through radiative-transfer atmospheric correction, then assess detectability limits for weak hydration-related absorptions in the 1.9–2.5 µm region.

Retrieve the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CTX single-frame EDR observation over the Columbia Hills region within Gusev Crater at ~6 m/pixel that can be used as a context/intensity basemap for pan-sharpening orbital spectral composites.

Retrieve the PDS4 context metadata record for the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Context Camera (CTX) instrument so I can link CTX image interpretation to the authoritative instrument description and mission context.

Identify the MRO HiRISE red-channel reduced-data-record observation that provides a map-quality basemap over the Columbia Hills and Home Plate area in Gusev Crater, suitable for equirectangular projection and precise registration of rover traverse and in-situ target locations.

Identify the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE Reduced Data Record (RDR) dataset (v1.1) that contains the red-channel products needed to build regional context mosaics and compare meter-scale ripple/outcrop geomorphology in and around Gusev Crater to rover-based observations.

Use Mars Global Surveyor TES calibrated thermal-infrared spectra acquired over the Gusev plains at ~3 km spatial scale to model surface thermophysical properties and assess how variable dust loading affects apparent basaltic surface signatures.

Use Mars Global Surveyor TES derived surface emissivity products over the Gusev plains at ~3 km spatial scale to perform spectral unmixing of mafic minerals versus ferric dust contributions and map regional compositional trends relevant to the plains–hills transition.

Assemble Mars Express OMEGA hyperspectral reflectance observations over the Gusev crater plains (regional scale) in the 0.4–5 µm range to quantify the spectral mixing between slightly oxidized basaltic sands and surface dust at ~350 m/pixel sampling.

Use Mars Express OMEGA derived global map products from 0.4–5 µm to place the Gusev crater plains spectral endmembers (mafic sands versus ferric-rich dust) into a planet-wide compositional context suitable for comparison with other low-albedo and dust-mantled regions.

Use MER Spirit Pancam calibrated multispectral imaging to quantify bedding geometry and stratigraphic relationships at the Voltaire outcrop exposure on Husband Hill in Gusev Crater during the mid-mission traverse (around sol 549), using an RDR mosaic suitable for photometric/spectral comparison across layers and clasts.

Identify the MER Spirit rover Pancam reduced-data-record (RDR) imaging volume that contains the calibrated multispectral products needed to build regional context mosaics and extract representative reflectance spectra for Columbia Hills materials spanning Husband Hill through the Inner Basin/Home Plate operations (roughly sols 500–1500).

For Mars Exploration Rover Spirit, identify the calibrated Navcam radiance products suitable for constructing panchromatic context mosaics in Gusev Crater (Columbia Hills) around the Voltaire outcrop campaign (approximately sol 551) to georeference Mini-TES footprint placements against local rock/soil units.

Locate the Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Navcam calibrated radiance archive covering the mission time span that includes the Columbia Hills traverse, so I can compare rover-scale geomorphic context and scene illumination across the mid-mission Husband Hill to Inner Basin transition without restricting to a single observation.

Locate the MER Spirit rover Hazard Avoidance Camera engineering image acquired on sol 605 at the Cliffhanger ripple near the head of Tennessee Valley on Husband Hill (Gusev Crater), documenting the ripple scuff experiment context for interpreting disturbed vs. undisturbed soil textures.

Locate the MER Spirit rover Hazard Avoidance Camera engineering image acquired on sol 710 at the El Dorado ripple field on the southeastern slope of Husband Hill (Gusev Crater), capturing the scuff disturbance context used to assess dark ripple morphology and aeolian surface properties.

Assemble a Spirit rover Microscopic Imager dataset suitable for quantifying clast morphology and matrix microtexture in Columbia Hills bedrock exposures at Gusev Crater (e.g., conglomeratic/impact-melt candidates on Husband Hill), emphasizing in-situ close-up frames that preserve mm-scale texture for grain-size and rounding statistics.

Compile Spirit rover Microscopic Imager products for quantitative grain-size and grain-shape analysis of platy, granular outcrops in the Columbia Hills (Low Ridge winter-campaign vicinity), prioritizing calibrated MI image products appropriate for measuring coarse sand-sized grains and resolving surface microrelief under variable illumination.

For the Mars Exploration Rover Spirit APXS investigation in Gusev Crater (Columbia Hills campaign), identify the archived APXS X-ray spectral measurements needed to derive elemental abundances for altered outcrops and aeolian materials encountered from the Husband Hill traverse into the Inner Basin.

For Mars Exploration Rover Spirit operations in the Columbia Hills (Gusev Crater), locate the APXS raw/engineering-level observations and associated instrument telemetry required to assess integration conditions and instrument performance during in-situ compositional measurements across outcrops, ripples, and disturbed soils.

For the Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Mössbauer Spectrometer in situ backscatter observations in Gusev crater (Columbia Hills), I need the raw spectra needed to independently refit Fe-bearing phase abundances (e.g., olivine, pyroxene, magnetite, hematite, goethite) and compute Fe3+/Fetotal for rocks and aeolian targets spanning Husband Hill through the Home Plate region.

To ground-truth orbital spectral interpretations over the Columbia Hills in Gusev crater, I need the Spirit rover Mössbauer Spectrometer summed spectra products suitable for extracting iron mineral assemblages and Fe3+/Fetotal ratios for representative altered outcrops and ripple-field materials in the Husband Hill–El Dorado–Low Ridge traverse corridor.

Assemble Spirit rover Mini-TES thermal-IR emissivity spectra (5–29 µm) acquired within Gusev Crater’s Columbia Hills to discriminate dust-dominated versus mafic sand surfaces and to derive spectral endmembers for altered/glassy outcrops relative to basaltic rocks.

Use Spirit rover Mini-TES brightness-temperature products for Columbia Hills observations in Gusev Crater to quantify surface temperature variability needed to convert radiance to emissivity consistently and to support thermal/near-IR radiative-transfer comparisons with orbital spectroscopy.

Assemble Opportunity rover Mini-TES averaged, mirror-dust–corrected thermal-IR emissivity spectra for Meridiani Planum rock targets (including Bounce Rock) to use as a pyroxene-dominated reference library for comparison against vesicular basalt spectra from other rover sites.

Extract Opportunity rover Mini-TES reduced-data (RDR) thermal emission spectra of Meridiani Planum rocks to independently verify the pyroxenite-like spectral shape of Bounce Rock and quantify pyroxene versus olivine contributions in the 5–29 µm region.
